subject: SLA exceptions & maintenance alignment — BlueRiver Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@blueriverpharma.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@blueriverpharma.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueRiver Order Form - SLA redlines

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement completed an initial pass on the Order Form + SLA and has a few redlines on uptime crediting and maintenance exceptions that they flagged as blockers for our internal counsel. High level: they want (1) clearer carveouts for scheduled maintenance windows (including a maximum monthly blackout), (2) a cap on aggregate service credits tied to calendar quarter revenue, and (3) a faster P1 response SLA with phone escalation listed explicitly.

I attached the PDF with inline redlines (BlueRiver_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). Can we get an updated position by EOD tomorrow? If it helps, we're open to a short call to walk the redlines.

Thanks,
Aditi Shah
Head of Procurement
BlueRiver Pharma
Attachments: BlueRiver_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@blueriverpharma.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BlueRiver Order Form - SLA redlines

Looping you all in — Aditi sent their redlines (attached). Key asks from BlueRiver: scheduled maintenance blackout cap, aggregate credit cap per quarter, explicit phone escalation for P1s.

Aditya — as AE can you lead pricing/credit concession discussions?
Laura — can you review the legal redlines for the maintenance carveout language and the aggregate credit cap? We should avoid an open liability that scales with unknowns.
Grace — can you confirm operational feasibility for a guaranteed phone escalation and whether we can commit to a tightened P1 response time (they're asking to move to 15 minutes acknowledgement instead of our standard 30).

I'll aim to draft a response with suggested compromises today; if anyone wants a quick sync, I can host a 20-min call at 3pm PT.

Thanks,
Michael
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@blueriverpharma.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BlueRiver Order Form - SLA redlines

Thanks Michael — quick notes from my side after reading the redlines: 

- Maintenance blackout: BlueRiver asks for a max of 8 hours/month of scheduled maintenance blackout (their language states a hard cap). Our standard practice is to allow a 72-hr rolling maintenance window per quarter (not per month). Compromise: we can offer no more than 12 hours/month with a 48-hr notice for planned blackouts and an annual calendar for known major updates.

- Aggregate credits: they want a cap at 20% of quarterly invoices. We should propose cap of 15% QTR rev or dollar-capped credits for predictable liability (e.g., smaller of 15% quarterly invoice or $250k per quarter).

- P1 response/phone escalation: ops says 30-min acknowledgement is standard. Grace — can we commit to a 15-min acknowledgement for P1s during business hours and provide an explicit phone escalation contact? If not, propose 15-min SLA with a limited phone escalation (first-line phone triage) and a follow-up within 2 hours.

I'll draft an email to Aditi with these three compromise positions and include a redline diff for the Order Form.

- Aditya
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLA_redline_diff.txt

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@blueriverpharma.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BlueRiver Order Form - SLA redlines

Thanks — read the redlines and Aditya's suggested compromises. A few legal notes to keep in the response: 

1) Maintenance carveouts: we should avoid a per-month hard cap that could hamper critical security patches. Suggested language: "Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed 12 cumulative hours per calendar month, subject to prior notice. Critical security updates may be deployed outside of the scheduled window when reasonably necessary; such deployments will not be counted against the scheduled maintenance cap."

2) Aggregate credit cap: proposed compromise acceptable but add a clause limiting credits to incidents where Redwood is the proximate cause of downtime (exclude upstream provider failures, client misconfiguration, or force majeure). 

3) P1 response: we can agree to 15-minute acknowledgement during customer-designated business hours provided the customer subscribes to the premium support add-on. Otherwise keep 30-minute SLA. If BlueRiver needs phone escalation as part of base support, price impact to be discussed.

I'll prepare redline text snippets; if Aditya sends the draft to Aditi I can append legal-friendly phrasing.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@blueriverpharma.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@blueriverpharma.com
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BlueRiver Order Form - SLA redlines (proposal)

Hi Aditi — thanks for the patience while we reviewed your redlines. Below is our proposed position (high level) — Laura, Aditya and Grace have reviewed and confirmed operational/legal feasibility. If this aligns, we can incorporate the attached redline diff and send to your counsel; otherwise happy to hop on a 30-min call.

Summary of proposed compromises: 

- Scheduled maintenance: Redwood proposes a cap of 12 cumulative hours per calendar month for scheduled maintenance with >=48 hours notice. Critical security updates required to remediate an active exploit are excluded from monthly cap and will be communicated promptly.

- Aggregate credits: Offer a cap equal to the lesser of 15% of quarterly invoice value or $250,000 per calendar quarter. Credits will only apply to downtime incidents where Redwood's infrastructure/services are the proximate cause; third-party provider failures, customer misconfiguration, and force majeure are excluded.

- P1 response & phone escalation: To include 15-minute acknowledgement and a phone escalation path, customer would need the premium support add-on (pricing to be included on Order Form). For customers who do not purchase premium support, standard 30-minute acknowledgement remains. For clarity, Redwood will provide a dedicated escalation phone number and 24/7 paging for premium support customers.

Next steps: if you confirm we are directionally aligned I will: (1) attach the redline diff (SLA_redline_diff.txt) and (2) prepare an updated Order Form for signature. We can also send via DocuSign (link below) once legal confirms.

Draft attachments: SLA_redline_diff.txt, BlueRiver_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf
DocuSign (prelim): https://app.docusign.com/envelope/0a1b2c3d4e5f
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345678/DEAL-2025-0742

Appreciate the collaboration — open to a call if you prefer to close verbally.

Best,
Michael Grant
